claims.title: Rock art at Tsodilo Hills
claims.summary: San hunter-gatherers paint the Tsodilo Hills; some images are dated to around 24,000 years before present, part of a record of over 4,500 paintings.

sources.label: Tsodilo Hills, Botswana — African Rock Art

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-24000bce-rock-art-at-tsodilo-hills, claim TL:BWA:event:24000bce:rock-art-at-tsodilo-hills, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Herders and farmers arrive
claims.summary: Peoples bringing cattle, sheep and pottery move into present-day Botswana, beginning the long shift from hunter-gathering toward herding and farming societies.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-1-herders-and-farmers-arrive, claim TL:BWA:event:1:herders-and-farmers-arrive, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Early Bantu settlement
claims.summary: Bantu-speaking settlers, among them the ancestors of the Kalanga, establish farming and cattle-keeping communities in the eastern part of the region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-200-early-bantu-settlement, claim TL:BWA:event:200:early-bantu-settlement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the Tswana merafe
claims.summary: The Bangwaketse form the first major Tswana state in the region, followed by the Bakwena, Bangwato and Batawana, cattle-keeping chiefdoms ruled by dikgosi.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-1750-rise-of-the-tswana-merafe, claim TL:BWA:event:1750:rise-of-the-tswana-merafe, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The difaqane convulses the region
claims.summary: Wars and forced migrations linked to the wider mfecane/difaqane disrupt Tswana society, bringing raiding, displacement and famine.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-1810-the-difaqane-convulses-the-region, claim TL:BWA:event:1810:the-difaqane-convulses-the-region, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sebego expels the Kololo
claims.summary: Sebego, regent of the Bangwaketse, raises some 4,000 men and permanently drives the invading Kololo out of the region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-1826-sebego-expels-the-kololo, claim TL:BWA:event:1826:sebego-expels-the-kololo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ndebele raids under Mzilikazi
claims.summary: Mzilikazi's Ndebele raid Tswana communities through the 1830s, capturing cattle, women and children before migrating north across the Limpopo.

sources.label: Matabeleland: The Ndebele Empire in Southern Africa

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-1837-ndebele-raids-under-mzilikazi, claim TL:BWA:event:1837:ndebele-raids-under-mzilikazi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: London Missionary Society arrives
claims.summary: LMS missionaries reach the Tswana lands; Robert Moffat later founds Kuruman and translates the Bible into Setswana.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-1816-london-missionary-society-arrives, claim TL:BWA:event:1816:london-missionary-society-arrives, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Livingstone founds Kolobeng
claims.summary: David Livingstone establishes the Kolobeng mission among the Bakwena near Kgosi Sechele, his only church and the source of his single convert.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-1845-livingstone-founds-kolobeng, claim TL:BWA:event:1845:livingstone-founds-kolobeng, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Boer attack on the Bakwena
claims.summary: Transvaal Boers attack Sechele's Bakwena and sack Livingstone's Kolobeng mission, part of mounting pressure from the Transvaal on Tswana land.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-1852-boer-attack-on-the-bakwena, claim TL:BWA:event:1852:boer-attack-on-the-bakwena, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Khama III becomes kgosi of the Bangwato
claims.summary: The Christian reformer Khama III takes the Bangwato chieftainship, banning liquor and aligning his powerful morafe with the missionaries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-1875-khama-iii-becomes-kgosi-of-the-bangwato, claim TL:BWA:event:1875:khama-iii-becomes-kgosi-of-the-bangwato, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bechuanaland Protectorate declared
claims.summary: After Sir Charles Warren's expedition, Britain proclaims a protectorate over the territory north of the Molopo to check Boer and German expansion.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-1885-bechuanaland-protectorate-declared, claim TL:BWA:event:1885:bechuanaland-protectorate-declared, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The three kings' mission to Britain
claims.summary: Khama III, Sebele I and Bathoen I travel to Britain and persuade the government to keep the protectorate out of Cecil Rhodes's British South Africa Company.

sources.label: William Charles Willoughby and the 1895 visit of the three kings

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-1895-the-three-kings-mission-to-britain, claim TL:BWA:event:1895:the-three-kings-mission-to-britain, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Capital moved to Mafeking
claims.summary: The protectorate's administration is seated at Mafeking, a town outside the territory's own borders, where it remains until the 1960s.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-1895-capital-moved-to-mafeking, claim TL:BWA:event:1895:capital-moved-to-mafeking, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Seretse Khama marries Ruth Williams
claims.summary: Bangwato heir Seretse Khama marries Englishwoman Ruth Williams in London, igniting a crisis with apartheid South Africa and Britain.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-1948-seretse-khama-marries-ruth-williams, claim TL:BWA:event:1948:seretse-khama-marries-ruth-williams, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Exile and return of Seretse Khama
claims.summary: Britain exiles Seretse and Ruth to appease South Africa; he is allowed home in 1956 after renouncing the Bangwato throne, fuelling nationalism.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-1950-exile-and-return-of-seretse-khama, claim TL:BWA:event:1950:exile-and-return-of-seretse-khama, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: BDP wins the first general election
claims.summary: Seretse Khama's Bechuanaland Democratic Party wins self-government elections; Gaborone is built as the new capital.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-1965-bdp-wins-the-first-general-election, claim TL:BWA:event:1965:bdp-wins-the-first-general-election, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence of Botswana
claims.summary: The protectorate becomes the Republic of Botswana with Seretse Khama as first president, entering nationhood as one of the world's poorest states.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-1966-independence-of-botswana, claim TL:BWA:event:1966:independence-of-botswana, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Diamonds discovered at Orapa
claims.summary: De Beers geologists locate a major diamond kimberlite pipe at Orapa, the find that would transform Botswana's economy.

sources.label: Diamonds to development: Botswana's post-independence economic growth

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-1967-diamonds-discovered-at-orapa, claim TL:BWA:event:1967:diamonds-discovered-at-orapa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Debswana partnership formed
claims.summary: Botswana and De Beers form a 50-50 joint venture to mine diamonds, securing for the state a direct share of mineral wealth.

sources.label: Diamonds to development: Botswana's post-independence economic growth

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-1969-debswana-partnership-formed, claim TL:BWA:event:1969:debswana-partnership-formed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Seretse Khama
claims.summary: Botswana's founding president dies in office; power passes peacefully to Vice-President Quett Masire, confirming the country's democratic stability.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Botswana: From the rock art of the Kalahari to a diamond democracy", terralore.co/country/BWA/chronicle#ev-1980-death-of-seretse-khama, claim TL:BWA:event:1980:death-of-seretse-khama, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
